title: Hackers raid OpenCode Console’s stored API keys, and the AI models its team turned to for defense refused to look at the malware
summary: OpenCode, the open-source AI coding agent gaining ground as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said attackers broke into an older system overnight and affected 1.4% of users of OpenCode Console, its online platform where some users keep the API keys they use for AI services. Developers posted OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google spend alerts firing overnight, with charges in the hundreds of dollars on individual accounts and a few totals above $1,000, TechCrunch reports. Anthropic and Google blocked the keys they believed were exposed; OpenAI worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund credits used in the attack, and OpenCode says refunds for unauthorized charges are underway. The open-source app and command-line tool were not affected, co-founder Dax Raad said. The harder lesson came mid-fight: Raad said attackers kept trying to get in for 48 hours, and the AI models his team used for analysis started refusing when the malicious code they were asked to examine tripped safety filters, until OpenCode got access to OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue program for vetted defensive security work. OpenCode has told affected users to revoke and replace their keys with each provider and says the incident remains ongoing.

title: A day after the U.S. removal order, DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the engine that runs its models in production
summary: DeepSeek released DeepInfer on Tuesday, October 20, publishing on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license the inference software it uses to serve its models at scale. For now it supports only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and runs on Nvidia SM100 data-center GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 chips, with optimized kernels, work split across many chips, speculative decoding, and structured outputs, The Next Web reports. It is not a complete service: the KV cache system, the split between prompt processing and answer generation, and load balancing across replicas are left out. DeepSeek says DeepInfer was first built mainly on vLLM and drew on SGLang and TensorRT-LLM; its speed figures are its own and have not been independently tested. The release came a day after U.S. civilian federal agencies were ordered to remove DeepSeek products, and the repository passed 8,000 GitHub stars by Tuesday afternoon.

title: OpenAI buys Orchestra Bio to put drug-development agents beside its Rosalind life-sciences models
summary: OpenAI said on Tuesday, October 20, that it has acquired Orchestra Bio, a platform where people and AI agents work together to coordinate drug programs, and is bringing its team and technology together with Rosalind, OpenAI’s models and tools for life-sciences research. Scientists and program leaders use Orchestra’s agents to monitor and track studies; when something breaks, such as a failed manufacturing batch that could delay a clinical trial, the agents identify which activities and timelines are affected and compare ways to respond, with people making the decision. OpenAI says new medicines take roughly 10 to 15 years from target discovery to U.S. approval, and that it wants agents that connect scientific findings to the studies and next steps needed to advance them. Terms were not disclosed.

title: Tech takes a breather and healthcare hits a record: the Dow jumps 1.02% while the S&P 500 adds 0.28% and the Nasdaq goes flat
summary: Wall Street rose on Tuesday, October 20, but not on AI. Healthcare led the S&P 500’s 11 sectors to a record high, with Eli Lilly the biggest index-point contributor, while the heavyweight technology sector eased 0.3% and was the biggest drag, keeping the Nasdaq close to flat after Monday’s rebound from last week’s AI-spending selloff, Reuters reports. The Dow rose 1.02%, the S&P 500 gained 0.28%, the Nasdaq lost 0.02%, and the small-cap Russell 2000 finished up 1.7%. “Equity investors are still a little skeptical around the AI trade and the ability for some of these companies to monetize their investments,” said Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors. Meta fell 1.6% and Alphabet 1%; Meta and Tesla report after Wednesday’s close.

title: SpaceX blows past estimates: revenue up 161% to $14.58 billion, with AI compute rental now its biggest business line
summary: SpaceX posted a third-quarter profit on Tuesday that blew past estimates, sending its shares up 2.5% in extended trading, Reuters reports. Revenue for the quarter ended September 30 rose 161% to $14.58 billion against an LSEG estimate of $12.72 billion, and net income was $4.4 billion versus a $1.1 billion loss a year earlier. AI revenue rose more than ninefold to $7.6 billion, mostly from renting computing capacity to developers such as Anthropic, Google, and Reflection AI rather than from its own models, but AI took $16.4 billion of $19.6 billion in capital spending, and the AI unit’s operating losses have been large. Starlink reached 13.6 million subscribers, above the 12.19 million expected, while average monthly revenue per subscriber has fallen to $69 from $99 in 2023.

title: Meta reports after the bell today, its first quarter since the Muse agent launch, with a 460% EPS jump expected
summary: Meta Platforms reports third-quarter results after Wednesday’s close, with a conference call at 4:30 p.m. Eastern (3:30 p.m. Central), CNBC’s earnings preview says. It is Meta’s first quarterly report since it released its AI agent Muse on September 8; the stock had risen more than 15% since that launch as of the preview, and LSEG data shows analysts expect earnings per share up 460% from a year earlier. History cuts both ways: Meta beats expectations 88% of the time, Bespoke data shows, but its shares fell nearly 8% after last quarter’s cash-flow hit and also dropped sharply after its Q1 2026 and Q3 2025 reports. Tesla reports after the bell too, with its call at 5:30 p.m. Eastern.

title: Mistral’s Voxtral 3 listens in 50+ languages, talks back with emotion, and runs a full voice agent in under a second a turn
summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3 on Tuesday, October 20: new speech-to-text and text-to-speech models plus a voice agent SDK, built on LiveKit, that streams listening, reasoning, tool calls, and speech in one pipeline so each turn completes in under a second and the agent stops talking when the caller cuts in. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 covers 50 languages with diarization and keyphrase biasing, and Mistral says it beats Whisper, Scribe v2, and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe; the 4B Mini costs $0.0035 a minute, and a realtime version runs under 500 milliseconds. Voxtral Mini TTS 3 adjusts emotion, pace, and emphasis across 35+ languages and 50+ dialects for $13 per million characters, and Pro Voice can adapt a speaker’s voice from 30 minutes of audio. It is available through Mistral’s API or for self-deployment.

title: NVIDIA’s new open Nemotron 3.5 Embed, Rerank, and Parse models help agents find the right page in fewer tokens
summary: NVIDIA released open, commercially available retrieval models on Wednesday, October 21: Nemotron 3.5 Embed in 8B and 1B sizes, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B, and the 631M-parameter Nemotron 3.5 Parse. Embed searches document text and images such as tables, charts, and schematics; the 8B model scored 61.17 nDCG@10 on ViDoRe v3.1, first among dense retrieval models, and the distilled 1B keeps 95.4% of that. In NVIDIA’s agent tests, adding the reranker cut agent token cost per query by about 14% while improving retrieval accuracy. Parse turns page images into structured Markdown and tables and ranks first on ParseBench among models under 1 billion parameters, at 10.5 pages per second on one H100. Weights are on Hugging Face.

title: Bria’s Fibo 2.0 generates and edits images in one open 8B model, and tops the open-weights editing arena
summary: Bria released Fibo 2.0, an 8B-parameter open-weights model that generates and edits images with one set of weights, plus a distilled four-step Edit Turbo checkpoint, ComfyUI Wiki reports. The model card cites an Artificial Analysis snapshot dated October 20 ranking it first among open-weights models in the image-editing arena, with an Elo of 1087, and second for text-to-image. New in 2.0: instruction edits that keep untouched regions intact, masked edits, and multi-reference edits with up to four images for cases like virtual try-on. It reads long structured JSON prompts rather than a sentence. The weights are gated on Hugging Face behind Bria’s terms, and core ComfyUI support is still pending.

title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, so PyTorch code runs natively on its TPUs with the tools developers already use
summary: Google said at PyTorch Conference 2026 on Tuesday, October 20, that TorchTPU, its native PyTorch stack for TPUs, is now open source on GitHub, making TPUs a native PyTorch option alongside GPUs and CPUs. Co-developed with Meta’s PyTorch team, it lets developers debug in eager mode and switch to torch.compile for production, and it plugs into vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, TorchTitan, Ray, and Hugging Face, where Transformers v5 can target TPUs with device_map="tpu". Google reports up to 52% model FLOPs utilization training Qwen 3 8B with near-linear scaling across up to 8,192 Ironwood TPUs. It arrives a day after Amazon’s TorchNeuron did the same for Trainium.

title: Mastercard opens Agent Pay for Machines to developers, so AI agents can pay for services within a set budget
summary: Mastercard opened Early Access to Agent Pay for Machines on Tuesday, October 20, giving developers the first version of its buyer- and seller-side APIs, a toolkit, sandbox, and documentation. Built on x402, an open protocol for requesting payment online, it works like this: a business gives an agent a job and a spending limit; when a paid service answers “402 Payment Required,” the agent signs a digital voucher within that limit, the provider verifies it and delivers, and vouchers are settled later. In a pilot demo at Cloudflare Connect, an agent for the marketing agency Hype bought social-media research from AIsa and eight campaign images through Cloudflare: nine payments, two merchants, one approved budget, and no separate accounts or API keys. It is still a pilot, and Mastercard is asking developers for feedback.

title: Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Ohio supercluster trained Muse and is headed toward about a million GPUs
summary: Meta on October 19 detailed Prometheus, the gigawatt-scale supercluster at its New Albany, Ohio, data center, AI Affairs reports. Its completed first phase, already hundreds of thousands of GPUs across several buildings, trained the Muse family, including Muse Wonder, and Meta is building toward roughly 1 million GPUs meant to work as one training system. Meta reports more than 85% goodput on Muse Wonder pre-training and more than 90% on reinforcement learning, meaning that share of time went into productive training, and a mean time between interruptions of about 47,000 GPU hours, raised past 54,000 after firmware fixes. Two years ago the site was handling ordinary web traffic.

title: Forty-eight hours under attack: when your tools stop helping, find better ones and keep going
summary: OpenCode’s team spent two days fending off nonstop break-in attempts, co-founder Dax Raad said, with AI defensive agents running around the clock. Then the models they leaned on for analysis started refusing, because the malicious code tripped safety filters. They did not quit; they got vetted access to OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue defensive-security program, and Raad said it improved their investigation, TechCrunch reports. The lesson for any hard week: when a tool stops working, that is a problem to solve, not a reason to stop. Name what is blocking you, ask for the access or help you need, and keep the work moving.

title: Build on others, then say so: DeepSeek credited vLLM, and vLLM thanked it back
summary: When DeepSeek opened its DeepInfer engine, it said the code was first built mainly on vLLM and drew on SGLang and TensorRT-LLM. The vLLM project thanked DeepSeek on X for crediting the open-source community and said it would keep improving its own support for V4.1-Flash with ideas from DeepInfer, The Next Web reports. Nobody builds alone. Learn from what others made, say where your ideas came from, and share what you learn back: credit costs nothing, and it turns a one-way borrow into a loop where everyone gets better.

summary: Magnolia Point hosts a Haunted Open House on Wednesday, October 21, from 5 to 7 p.m. at 104 Marblehead Ave., Lafayette, according to One Acadiana’s community calendar. Entry is free and costumes are encouraged.

summary: Windborne’s The Music of the Rolling Stones plays the Heymann Performing Arts Center, 1373 S. College Rd., on Thursday, October 22, at 7:30 p.m., the Heymann Center’s schedule shows. summary: Downtown Lafayette’s free lunchtime concert series Bach Lunch returns to Parc Sans Souci, 201 E. Vermilion St., on Friday, October 23. Food vendors start selling at 11 a.m. and Lafayette singer-songwriter Amelie Cecile and her four-piece band play from noon to 1 p.m., Downtown Lafayette Unlimited says. summary: Country singer Zach Top plays the Lafayette Cajundome on Friday, October 23, at 8 p.m. on his Cold Beer & Country Music Tour 2026, with Lukas Nelson also on the lineup, Live Nation’s event page shows.

title: Saturday: Trick-or-Treat at the Boo-seum, Lafayette Science Museum, noon to 3 p.m.
summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum, 433 Jefferson St., turns October’s STEM Saturday into Trick-or-Treat at the BOO-seum on Saturday, October 24, from noon to 3 p.m. Costume contest judging runs noon to 1:30 p.m., with winners announced at 2 p.m. in four categories: Best Overall, Most Scientific, Spookiest, and Silliest. Expect Halloween STEM activities at indoor trick-or-treat stations, a mini pumpkin scavenger hunt, and costumed members of the 501st Legion’s local Bast Alpha Garrison. All activities are included with regular museum admission; all ages welcome.

title: Sunday: “The Original” Pine Leaf Boys reunite at Hideaway on Lee, 7 to 9 p.m.
summary: Hideaway on Lee, 407 Lee Ave., hosts “The Original” Pine Leaf Boys on Sunday, October 25, from 7 to 9 p.m.: a night of the tunes that started the band, with Cedric Watson, Wilson Savoy, and Jean Bertrand, the venue’s listing says. Lafayette Travel’s weekly rundown calls it an evening of stripped-down French music.
